stem: According to the line graph, during which of the following time periods did the number of performances increase the most?
stimulus: A musicologist tracked how often a little-known Baroque composer's works were performed in concert each year. The line graph shows year on the horizontal axis and number of performances on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (2016, 14), (2017, 18), (2018, 31), (2019, 27), (2020, 9), (2021, 20), and (2022, 30).
explanation: The question asks about an increase, so you only look at segments that go up and compare how much each one rises. From 2016 to 2017 the number rises by 18 − 14 = 4. From 2017 to 2018 it rises by 31 − 18 = 13. The other two choices are decreases, so 2017 to 2018 has the greatest increase.

A.why: Performances did increase from 2016 to 2017, but only by 4. You found an increase without checking that it was the greatest. The rise from 2017 to 2018 is 13.

C.why: You picked the period with the highest values on the graph (31 and 27). The question asks about the change across each period, and from 2018 to 2019 the number actually went down by 4.

D.why: 2019 to 2020 has the steepest segment on the graph, but it goes down. That drop of 18 is the greatest decrease, and the question asks for the greatest increase.

stem: According to the line graph, on which day was the tensile strength of the strip the least?
stimulus: A materials scientist left a strip of plant-based plastic outdoors and tested its tensile strength once a day for a week. The line graph shows day on the horizontal axis and tensile strength, in megapascals (MPa), on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (1, 42), (2, 39), (3, 44), (4, 36), (5, 31), (6, 38), and (7, 33).
explanation: You need the lowest point on the graph. The lowest tensile strength is 31 MPa, and it was measured on day 5.

A.why: Day 3 is the highest point on the graph, at 44 MPa. The question asks when the strength was the least, not the greatest.

B.why: Day 4 is the bottom of the steepest drop (from 44 to 36 MPa). You looked for the biggest decrease instead of the lowest value. Strength kept falling after day 4, down to 31 MPa on day 5.

D.why: Day 7 is low at 33 MPa, but you treated it as the minimum without checking it against day 5. Day 5, at 31 MPa, is lower.

stem: According to the line graph, in which year did the excavation team recover 85 artifacts?
stimulus: An archaeological team excavated the same hillside site every summer and counted the artifacts recovered each season. The line graph shows year on the horizontal axis and number of artifacts recovered on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (2015, 45), (2016, 70), (2017, 55), (2018, 85), (2019, 110), (2020, 65), and (2021, 90).
explanation: Find 85 on the vertical axis, move across to the point at that height, and read the year below it. The point at 85 artifacts is above 2018.

A.why: 2017 is where the segment that climbs to 85 begins. You read the year at the wrong end of that segment. In 2017 the team recovered only 55 artifacts.

C.why: 2019 is the highest point on the graph, at 110 artifacts. The question asks for the year with a specific value, 85, not for the maximum.

D.why: The 2021 point is at 90, one gridline above 85. You read its height too loosely. The point that is exactly at 85 is above 2018.

stem: According to the line graph, during which of the following time periods did the number of printed road maps decrease the most?
stimulus: A national mapping agency recorded how many paper road maps it printed each year as more drivers switched to phone navigation. The line graph shows year on the horizontal axis and number of maps printed, in thousands, on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (2012, 48), (2013, 44), (2014, 47), (2015, 34), (2016, 29), (2017, 36), and (2018, 30).
explanation: Compare how far each downward segment drops. From 2014 to 2015 the number falls by 47 − 34 = 13 thousand. From 2015 to 2016 it falls by 5 thousand, and from 2017 to 2018 by 6 thousand. The greatest decrease is from 2014 to 2015.

B.why: 2016 is the lowest point on the graph, so the segment from 2015 to 2016 ends at the smallest value. But it drops only 34 − 29 = 5 thousand. You compared where segments end instead of how much they change.

C.why: From 2016 to 2017 the number went up by 7 thousand. That is the greatest increase on the graph, and the question asks for the greatest decrease.

D.why: Printing did decrease from 2017 to 2018, but only by 6 thousand. You found a decrease without checking that it was the largest. The drop from 2014 to 2015 is 13 thousand.

stem: According to the line graph, during which of the following time periods did the mean daily fiber intake change the most?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers asked participants in a seven-week study to log everything they ate, and calculated the group's mean daily fiber intake for each week. The line graph shows week on the horizontal axis and mean daily fiber intake, in grams, on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (1, 18), (2, 21), (3, 19), (4, 26), (5, 24), (6, 15), and (7, 17).
explanation: The question says change, so increases and decreases both count. Compare the size of each segment's rise or drop. From week 5 to week 6 the intake falls by 24 − 15 = 9 grams. That is larger than the 7-gram rise from week 3 to week 4 and larger than every other change.

A.why: Week 3 to week 4 is the greatest increase, at 7 grams. But you only looked at increases. The question asks for change in either direction, and the 9-gram drop from week 5 to week 6 is bigger.

B.why: Weeks 4 and 5 have the highest values on the graph (26 and 24 grams). Intake changed by only 2 grams between them. You compared the values themselves instead of the change between them.

D.why: You found the lowest point, week 6, which is near the big change. Then you picked the segment that starts there instead of the one that ends there. From week 6 to week 7 the intake rises by only 2 grams.

stem: According to the line graph, in which year was the number of vacant storefronts the least?

The line graph shows year on the horizontal axis and number of vacant storefronts on the vertical axis. The graph has 7 data points connected by line segments. The data points have the following coordinates: (2017, 24), (2018, 19), (2019, 21), (2020, 33), (2021, 28), (2022, 16), and (2023, 18).
explanation: You need the lowest point on the graph. The fewest vacant storefronts, 16, were counted in 2022.

A.why: 2018 is a low point compared with the years on either side of it, at 19. But you stopped at the first dip. The count goes lower in 2022, down to 16.

B.why: 2020 is the highest point on the graph, at 33 vacant storefronts. The question asks for the least, not the greatest.

C.why: 2021 is where the steepest drop begins (from 28 to 16). You looked for the biggest decrease instead of the lowest value, and then picked the start of that segment instead of where it ends.
